title: JavaScript Mini Project
description: Synthesize Module 1-3 fundamentals into a resilient, production-ready learner progress tracker handling calculations, filtering, formatting, and edge cases.

objectives.statement: Architect a multi-function data processing pipeline combining objects, arrays, loops, conditionals, and functions.
Implement defensive edge-case handling for empty collections, boundary scores, and zero-progress states.
Generate formatted user-facing progress summaries from calculated application state.

content.title: Module 1-3 Capstone: Forge Learner Progress Tracker
content.hook: You have mastered variables, operators, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, and objects. Now, connect them into a complete application.
content.context: In this capstone, you will construct a modular JavaScript progress engine. You will model learner records and lesson collections, implement helper functions to add lessons, count completed units, compute completion percentages defensively, filter remaining tasks, and produce a polished summary report.
goals: Model learner and lesson entities cleanly using objects and arrays.
Compose single-responsibility functions to process application state.
Defensively guard against zero-length arrays and boundary edge cases.

content.title: Capstone Pipeline Architecture
content.description: Visual flow showing raw tracker state { name, lessons: [...] } flowing into countCompleted(), feeding calculateProgressPercentage() with a zero-division guard, passing into getIncompleteLessons() with filter(!completed), and composing into generateLearnerSummary().

feedback.correct: Spot on! Composing programs from small, testable functions isolates bugs, enables code reuse, and simplifies edge-case handling.
feedback.incorrect: Modular functions make software easier to test, debug, and maintain compared to monolithic scripts.

hints.content: Modular code allows each calculation to be verified and tested independently.

content.question: Why is it best engineering practice to build this capstone by writing and testing small, individual helper functions rather than writing one massive script all at once?

options.text: Small functions can be tested in isolation, prevent code duplication, and allow edge cases (like empty arrays) to be debugged immediately.
JavaScript performance slows down significantly if a single file has more than 50 lines of code.
Monolithic scripts cannot access JavaScript array methods like map or filter.
The JavaScript browser engine forbids calling more than one loop inside a single function.

feedback.correct: Magnificent! You completed the Module 1-3 capstone with full defensive safeguards, structured data models, and clean composed functions.
feedback.incorrect: Check your logic: ensure calculateProgressPercentage returns 0 on empty lessons, getIncompleteLessons returns titles of incomplete lessons, and generateLearnerSummary formats the remaining string correctly.

content.title: Build the Forge Progress Engine
content.prompt:
Implement the complete set of progress tracker functions:
1. createTracker(name, initialLessons): Returns `{ name, lessons: initialLessons || [] }`.
2. addLesson(tracker, lesson): Appends lesson to tracker.lessons and returns tracker.
3. countCompleted(tracker): Returns the number of lessons where `completed === true`.
4. calculateProgressPercentage(tracker): Returns Math.round((completed / total) * 100). If total is 0, defensively return 0.
5. getIncompleteLessons(tracker): Returns an array of lesson titles (strings) for lessons where `completed === false`.
6. generateLearnerSummary(tracker): Returns string: `"[Learner Name] — [Percent]% complete ([Completed]/[Total] lessons). Remaining: [Titles joined by comma or 'None']"`.

feedback.correct: Well reflected! Clean data models and small composed functions make application code robust, scalable, and delightful to maintain.
feedback.incorrect: Please provide at least 30 characters reflecting on how composing functions and modeling data structures improves software design.

content.title: Module 1-3 Capstone Complete
